title: Recovered Phase 6G surface-parser compatibility fixtures
purpose: Preserve source-backed positive and negative cases from the archived Phase 6G prototype before any integration into the TypeScript workbench.

source.evidenceType: archived prototype report and source; reported test outcomes are historical, not current CI evidence

notation.name: phase-6g-prototype-surface-notation
notation.description: Whitespace-tokenised romanised tokens with fixed-arity head-initial expressions. Not the Phase 2 angle-bracket audit notation.
notation.aliasStatus: historically documented prototype aliases; not a global canon rewrite

cases.label: integer numeral with explicit unit
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: numeral consists of digit tokens followed by a unit.

cases.label: decimal numeral with explicit decimal marker
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: optional SHI decimal fraction precedes the unit.

cases.label: numeral missing unit closure
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: every numeral must end in a unit; SHO closes dimensionless numerals.

cases.label: decimal marker without following fractional digit
cases.evidence: Recovered source requires at least one digit after SHI.

cases.label: digit sequence closed by SHO as binding identifier
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: binding identifiers are numerals closed by SHO.

cases.label: binding identifier without SHO closure
cases.evidence: Recovered source requires binding identifiers to end in SHO.

cases.label: nested fixed-arity arithmetic
cases.input: FRAPA KI SHO FRAPA TO SHO MU SHO
cases.evidence: Phase 6G uses head-initial fixed arity, without commas or angle brackets. Fixture is a structural target; verify exact token semantics against the source parser before execution.
cases.notes: Do not interpret acceptance as type correctness or spell feasibility.

cases.label: control form with explicit block delimiters
cases.input: BEK GRAN ZA SHO TO SHO METO FRAPA KI SHO TO SHO DOGU
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: control forms take a condition followed by a block opened by METO and closed by DOGU.
cases.notes: Operand spelling and operator signature are intentionally flagged for direct validation; do not use as canonical example.

cases.label: control form missing METO
cases.input: BEK GRAN ZA SHO TO SHO FRAPA KI SHO TO SHO DOGU
cases.evidence: Phase 6G reported tests cover missing METO rejection.

cases.label: control form missing DOGU
cases.input: BEK GRAN ZA SHO TO SHO METO FRAPA KI SHO TO SHO
cases.evidence: Phase 6G reported tests cover missing DOGU rejection.

cases.label: ambiguous RE in numeral context
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: RE/RA homophones across digit, unit and reference uses; fail closed when ambiguous.

cases.label: ambiguous RA in numeral context
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report: RA has unit/reference collision and requires slot-sensitive disambiguation.

cases.label: operator with unresolved signature
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report says NES and other incomplete signatures are rejected rather than guessed.

cases.label: legacy arithmetic alias normalisation
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report documents FRATA to FRAJA as a legacy alias.

cases.label: block delimiter outside a control form
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report records this rejection among its 19 historical tests.

cases.label: syntactic acceptance does not imply semantic or physical validity
cases.evidence: Phase 6G report explicitly states that parsed expressions may still be ill-typed, unevaluable, physically infeasible, or invalid mana constructions.

mustNotClaim: that archived Python test results are current CI results
that a parsed expression is canonical Arcane
that syntax success implies type correctness, physical feasibility, or spell validity
executionPolicy.nextStep: Implement a separate Phase 6G parser adapter or test harness, then execute these cases against that implementation and record per-case outputs without changing canon.
